title: Deuterium-Enhanced Photoluminescence and Magnetic Properties in Octanuclear Terbium(III) Complexes Containing a Hexadentate N2O4-Type Ligand

material_class.structural_family: octanuclear Tb8 cluster with four corner-sharing incomplete cuboidal {Tb3O4} cores

synthesis.procedure: H2dpim (56 mg, 0.15 mmol) was dissolved in ethanol (5 mL). Terbium(III) nitrate pentahydrate (65 mg, 0.15 mmol) was dissolved in ethanol (2 mL) and added dropwise to the ligand solution. The transparent solution was stirred for 1 h at room temperature. Diethyl ether was allowed to diffuse into the solution for several days, yielding transparent colorless single crystals of 1, which were collected by filtration, washed with diethyl ether, and dried in air.
synthesis.time: stirred 1 h; diethyl ether diffusion for several days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction followed by diethyl ether vapor diffusion crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: ether diffusion yielded colorless single crystals; filtered, washed with diethyl ether, dried in air

properties.summary: Strong Tb(III) photoluminescence (488–620 nm) with relative quantum yield Φ1 = 19% in MeCN. Solid-state χMT is 92.7 emu K mol−1 at room temperature and falls to 57.2 emu K mol−1 at ~6 K; magnetization is 38.6 Nβ at 2 K and 5 T. No frequency-dependent ac susceptibility or SMM behavior.

material_class.structural_family: isostructural octanuclear Tb8 cluster with four corner-sharing incomplete cuboidal {Tb3O4} cores (OD-bridged)

synthesis.procedure: H2dpim (56 mg, 0.15 mmol) was dried at 110 °C for 2 h and dissolved in ethanol/deuterium oxide (4 mL, 3/1 v/v). Dehydrated terbium(III) nitrate (52 mg, 0.15 mmol; obtained by heating Tb(NO3)3·5H2O in vacuum at 118 °C for 25 h) was dissolved in ethanol/deuterium oxide (2 mL, 1/1 v/v) and added dropwise to the ligand solution. The transparent solution was stirred for 1 h at room temperature. Diethyl ether was allowed to diffuse into the solution for several days, yielding transparent colorless single crystals of 2, which were collected by filtration, washed with diethyl ether, and dried in air.

properties.summary: Deuteration of the eight hydroxo bridges strongly enhances Tb(III) photoluminescence (488–620 nm), giving Φ2 = 75% in MeCN (~4-fold higher than 1). Magnetic data show χMT = 93.5 emu K mol−1 at room temperature, decreasing more than in 1 to 53.2 emu K mol−1 at ~6 K, consistent with Stark-level depopulation and slightly stronger antiferromagnetic contributions. Magnetization is 36.3 Nβ at 2 K and 5 T; no SMM behavior.
